subject: Prefetch hit-rate plan, pricing assumptions & next steps
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Liu <anna.liu@fincloud.io>, Tim O'Leary <tim.oleary@fincloud.io>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Prefetch hit-rate plan, pricing assumptions & next steps

Hi Anna / Tim — great conversation this morning. Quick post-call recap focused on the pricing assumptions we discussed and the two quick asks to move the pilot forward. I saved the detailed hit-rate workbook as an attachment (fincloud_hitrate_model_v1.xlsx).

Call highlights (as we captured):
- Expected steady-state token volume: 20M–50M tokens / month in months 2–6 (peak burst to ~75M for event-driven periods).
- Procurement guidance: target monthly budget range you mentioned was $40k–$120k (you flagged $120k as the absolute upper band if we can meet latency/ops SLAs).
- Prefetch/prefix cache strategy: you plan to precompute/commonize the top ~60% of conversational prefixes (auth & navigation flows) and hold a warm prefix layer for 24–48 hours for active users. Team estimate: 30–45% hit rate in month 1, trending toward 45–55% if we expand coverage to more flows.

Pricing assumptions I used in the attached workbook:
- Baseline list (selected model variant) = $700 / 1M tokens.
- Cache-hit effective unit for a hit = $0. (we treat hits as served from cached outputs / local KV so token compute is avoided for those tokens)
- Effective $/1M tokens = baseline * (1 - hit_rate). Example: at 40% hit -> 700 * 0.60 = $420 / 1M effective.

Quick sensitivity rows are in the workbook but the headline items for the pilot:
1) If we can achieve ~40% hit rate on the pilot cohort, your effective unit price will be ~ $420 / 1M tokens.
2) For 20M–50M tokens / month that converts to an expected monthly compute bill range of $8.4k – $21k (before negotiated discounts/commits).
3) To meet your $40k–$120k procurement target we should talk about committed reserved capacity + a pilot commit that includes a small one-time onboarding fee and a short-term unit discount.

Next steps I propose (simple and actionable):
- Anna: confirm the 20M–50M monthly range and whether the 24–48h warm residency is feasible on your side (we can mirror based on session ids).
- Tim / Procurement: share any standard SOW terms you need; procurement@ was copied for transparency.
- Internal: Rafael / Monica — please review the attached workbook and the quick pilot price band I outlined below; I’ll follow up with a proposed pilot SOW once we align on hit-rate and commit level.

Pilot price band I modeled (in workbook):
- Pilot (3 months): committed 20M/mo -> list-based effective $/1M at 35% hit = $455; with a 10% pilot discount -> $409 / 1M effective.
- Scale target (after pilot): committed 50M/mo -> with 45% hit -> $385 / 1M effective; contract discount tiers available.

Attachments: fincloud_hitrate_model_v1.xlsx (hit-rate sensitivity + cost sheet).

If you’re good with this framing I’ll lock the pilot terms and get a short SOW over to procurement.

Thanks,
Priya
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priya@redwood.ai
[attachment: fincloud_hitrate_model_v1.xlsx (Excel)]

From: Anna Liu <anna.liu@fincloud.io>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tim O'Leary <tim.oleary@fincloud.io>, procurement@fincloud.io
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 12:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Prefetch hit-rate plan, pricing assumptions & next steps

Thanks, Priya — appreciate the concise recap and workbook. A few quick confirmations from our side: 

- Volume: 20M–50M tokens / month is the right operational band for months 2–6. We expect a one-time onboarding spike (events) that could push to ~80M for up to two weeks.
- Warm residency: 24 hours is the target we can commit to for pilot users; looking to expand to 48 hours if the pilot shows clear hit-rate lift without privacy concerns.
- Procurement constraint: the $40k–$120k band stands. For the pilot we’ll need a clear line item in the SOW for a month-to-month cap and an explicit rollback if latency exceeds 400ms p95.

Two asks for the pilot SOW you mentioned: 
1) Can you include a simple SLA clause for p95 latency (target < 400ms, credit if > 500ms)?
2) We require a brief security addendum referencing SOC2 evidence — procurement will not sign without that in the packet.

I’ve looped in procurement@ — Tim, can you confirm acceptance of the pilot approach and whether you need a vendor questionnaire before SOW?

Thanks,
Anna
Anna Liu
Head of Product, FinCloud
anna.liu@fincloud.io

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anna Liu <anna.liu@fincloud.io>, Tim O'Leary <tim.oleary@fincloud.io>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 10:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Prefetch hit-rate plan, pricing assumptions & next steps — internal thread

Rafael / Monica — forwarding Anna’s confirmation. Two internal asks so we can respond with an SOW by EOD Tue: 

1) Confirm pilot pricing approval: workbook suggests a 3‑month pilot at committed 20M/mo with 10% pilot discount (effective ~ $409 / 1M assuming 35% hit). Can we approve offering this band and include a $15k onboarding credit tied to SOC2 artifact delivery?

2) SLA language and fallback: Procurement asked for p95 < 400ms and credit if > 500ms. We should also include an automatic fallback to a lower-cost model variant (compatible with quality) if our GPU pool experiences sustained latency > 600ms for 30+ minutes. Rafael — can you confirm acceptable credit structure (% of monthly invoice) and fallback model variants to include?

I attached a short playbook page with the rollout controls and our recommended legal bullets (redwood_prefetch_playbook.pdf). If we sign off I’ll produce a one-page SOW + security addendum and route to procurement.

Action items:
- Rafael: approve pilot discount and credit numbers, and confirm fallback model names.
- Monica: prepare ops runbook snippet (cache residency tuning + monitoring hooks) to include in SOW.

Thanks,
Priya
[attachment: redwood_prefetch_playbook.pdf (PDF)]

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anna Liu <anna.liu@fincloud.io>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Prefetch hit-rate plan, pricing assumptions & next steps — internal thread

Priya — good framing. I approve the 10% pilot discount and the $15k onboarding credit tied to SOC2 artifact delivery. For the SLA credit structure propose: 
- If p95 latency > 500ms for more than 15 minutes during a billing period, credit 2% of the monthly compute invoice.
- If p95 latency > 700ms for sustained 30+ minutes, credit 5% and trigger immediate fallback to the lower-cost model variant.

Fallback model variants to call out (for legal/ops):
- primary: redwood-llama-13b-quant (selected model)
- fallback: redwood-llama-7b-quant (lower compute, slightly higher prompt-fusion risk)

Monica — please assemble the ops snippet for the SOW (cache residency config + a short monitoring dashboard screenshot) and drop it in the shared doc. Priya — once those two bullets are in I’m happy for you to send SOW to procurement.

— Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Director, Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
